correctness.rationale: For every slice of the arbitrary-index \(\ell_p\)-sum, the proof converts the norm-one dual profile to a norm-one positive \(\ell_p\) profile and uses componentwise Daugavet witnesses. The scaling lemma is proved explicitly. The remaining scalar infimum is exact by monotonicity of \(F(t)=(1+t)^p-t^p\), and a coordinate-supported slice gives the reverse inequality. Boundary cases \(z=0\), a singleton index set, zero coordinates, and infinite index sets are included. No finite experiment substitutes for the infinite-dimensional argument.

value.rationale: The formula completely localizes a recently introduced quantitative invariant on a natural direct-sum class. It identifies the smallest coordinate norm as the exact finite-sum control parameter and shows that arbitrary infinite index cardinality forces a flat sphere profile \(2^{1/p}\). This is structural information not recoverable from the known global thickness constant alone.
